results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 38 outliner summaries match the controlling idea of the aligned spec unit, in spec order; the three callouts map to the roadmap, the thesis statement and the book's failure-pattern callout (no spec paragraph).

Only 'Questions to Ask ¶2' was marked two_ideas (recap + hand-off). The recap ('You can now say that it reported the fifth of twelve steps...') is the declared callback and supplies the carry-over of the hand-off's contrast (a payment Mila started and her bank approved), so it supports the controlling idea of p35 rather than competing with it.

Every unit ties to a supporting claim: intro and scene to the thesis and S1; the two-seconds stretch to S2; the days and books stretches to S3; the step table to S1/S3; the Stripe section to S4; the silent losses and the conclusion to S5.

Each table and figure is explained by its lead-in paragraph or the paragraph after it (the step table by 'Now read the table downward...', the Stripe table by the replay and 'As a result, the record an integration waits for differs at three hand-offs', the loss table by its lead-in and 'To catch these'); figure captions state what each shows; quotations are followed or preceded by a sentence drawing the point (e.g. 'The provider has promised that it sent the money.').

Every declared transition_in is expressed at its boundary: sequence openings ('What the request carries next', 'Once the token arrives', 'Money follows the record'), contrasts ('This step, unlike the third', 'The twelfth is different', 'Everything above went right'), conclusion_summary ('So the Payment successful... reports step five alone', 'Set side by side'), example ('For example, replay the pass'), cause_effect ('As a result'), problem_solution ('To catch these'), and the conclusion's labelled phrases ('Established.', 'Depends on context.', 'The author's synthesis.').

Terms the flow readers flagged (Keel codes, sales day, batch, balance account, exemption, liability shift, Custom connected accounts, destination charge) are on audience.already_knows (Parts I-VIII mechanisms; Larkfield and Keel from meet-larkfield); the two does_not_know items (the record each step leaves on each provider; where an approved payment is lost silently) are both given by the draft. Cold-reader stumbles on these terms are recorded under flow_is_followable.
Opens on a puzzling scenario (the true 'Payment successful' at 19:42 reporting the fifth of twelve steps), not a placeholder, restated question, definition, 'dawn of man' or book report.

Conclusion sorts what is established, what depends on context and the author's synthesis, then questions and a hand-off; it adds no new subtopic, does not end on a restated thesis and holds no body evidence.

'The three stretches are three kinds of evidence... so the truth of a payment is in the comparison at the twelfth' states what no single section states, and 'I would spend first at the hand-offs: one reference..., one unconfirmed state, a sweep, a daily match' plus the per-provider 'which record justifies a state' bullet answers the so-what.

'At 19:42 the screen said the payment had succeeded. You can now say that it reported the fifth of twelve steps, name the seven that followed...' returns to the 'Payment successful' message and the question of which step it reported, up to 25 March and the window open until July.

The intro reader predicted all seven sections in order (Larkfield's records, three stretches, the step table, the Stripe replay, the silent losses), the evidence (one dated worked example, provider records, a table, cross-references) and the tone. Minor: the reader placed the payout in the 'two days' stretch and was unsure which steps fall in which stretch, because ¶5 names the stretches without their steps.

Reader names all four expected loss points (approval expiring before a delayed capture; CAPTURE_FAILED after capture; funds set off or held at funding; payout returned), the record that shows each on Adyen and Stripe, and the remedy of a 'promised, not yet confirmed' state with a sweep and a daily reconciliation.

Reader gives two correct differences: the outcome (Adyen result code then AUTHORISATION webhook, no Checkout API call that reads the payment back; Stripe PaymentIntent retrievable by ID) and the funds (Adyen sales-day batch after the settlement delay; Stripe per-transaction pending to available_on, 12 March), and adds the capture difference.

All twelve rows of the step table name a party, a message or record, a promise and a failure with a [[...]] link to the owning chapter of Parts I-VIII; the two deliberate absences (row 6 'None of its own when automatic', row 12 'None: this step checks the others') are stated, not blank.
